_doc: The town's script (townsfolk step 8, #1144; docs/briefs/townsfolk.md §5 'What they say'). The same shape as no_law.json (docs/scripts/README.md): `cast` the pools (townsfolk share pools by type, DESIGN §9; cast ids shared with no_law.json keep one voice), `scenes` with `lines` (id, speaker, trigger, when, condition, delivery, words, takes). Lines may hold slots in braces ({who}, {whom}, {where}, {shots}, {teller}); a scene's `reads` says which code reads it. The `runner` and `news` scenes are read by the game now (TownScript, src/people/town_script.gd; a wording `built` is what the game said before this file, kept); the rest wait for step 9's line picker. Every wording is PROPOSED and nothing is voiced until Sean taps Script OK. No line here says Harlan's name. No Law's town, morning and funeral lines stay in no_law.json and aren't repeated.
title: The town
mission: none: the town between and after the missions (townsfolk #850, step 8)
status: written 2026-11-22 (#1144): waiting on Sean's Script OK
sources: docs/briefs/townsfolk.md §5 (the line table, how the town treats Harlan), §10 (Sean's picks 2-4, #851)
src/people/fetch_help.gd FetchHelp.LINES, src/people/town_news.gd line_of (the placeholders these replace)
notes: Harlan doesn't speak; nobody here names him.
Secrets: the news only carries what a townsman sensed, so K2-K4 can't leak; nobody in town names the prisoner (K3) or the Baron (K4).
Variants per line, picked by the speaker's seed (the playtest's 'Three shots, I counted.' three times).

facts.set_by: C8 a, when Sean nods on #830

kept.words: Doc! Man down, out front of {where}. / A man's down.
kept.why: Built (the game's placeholder before this script). The blind reader heard police and army talk in 'man down'; the new wordings say 'a man's hurt' and 'took bad'. For Sean: drop the built ones if he agrees.

kept.why: The reader called it a neat writer's button but close to good; kept for Sean to say.

cast.name: A townsman
cast.bible: P·bible (No Law's Beat 1, the town without a sheriff)
cast.brief: Forties, a storekeeper type; worried, talks low, glances over his shoulder.

cast.name: A townswoman
cast.brief: Thirties to forties, plain-spoken, good grammar; brisk, says what she thinks.

cast.name: A bold man in the street
cast.bible: No Law's Beat 1: 'others behave more boldly'
cast.brief: Thirties, a teamster or a hand in town; too loud, a little drunk, enjoying the sheriff's absence.

cast.name: The barkeep
cast.brief: Forties, aggrieved and quick, always counting what a thing costs him; a nasal Midwestern voice that rises when he's upset.

cast.name: The undertaker
cast.brief: Sixties, unhurried, precise, a dry gallows humour he doesn't know he has.

cast.name: The doctor
cast.bible: VOICES.md, The doctor (the same voice as in the sheriff's script)
cast.brief: Late forties, an educated Easterner; brisk, quiet, dry.

cast.name: The storekeeper
cast.brief: Fifties, a Missouri man, careful with money and with words; polite to the penny. Says less when he's frightened, not more.

cast.name: The hotel's landlady
cast.brief: Forties, a widow who runs the hotel; brisk, plain, has fed worse men than these. Never raises her voice.

cast.name: The liveryman
cast.brief: Fifties, horse-sense and no patience; counts feed in nickels (#1184).

cast.name: The smith
cast.brief: Forties, big and slow-spoken; proud of his iron, shy of his letters (#1184).

cast.name: The drifter
cast.brief: Twenties, out of work and easy about it; rode in from nowhere much (#1184).

cast.name: The saloon girl
cast.brief: Twenties, quick and tired; teases, sizes a man up by his purse (#1184).

scenes.title: The runner
scenes.when: Any day, a man down in town
scenes.reads: FetchHelp (src/people/fetch_help.gd): the most specific id that has words first (runner.shot, then runner); a wording by the runner's own seed. {where} is FetchHelp.place_name: 'the store', 'the saloon', 'Doc's'.
scenes.setting: A townsman who saw a man go down runs for the doctor (or, once there's a deputy, for Harlan), tells him on arrival, and hands over his version of the news.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He starts for the doctor's (Reaction's runner)
lines.delivery: Called back over his shoulder as he goes. The first words are to the others.

words.text: I'll get Doc! Don't move him.
I'll go. Don't move him.
Somebody fetch Doc... I'll go!
Leave him lay. I'm going for Doc.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He starts for Harlan (the badge given, Harlan seen in town)
lines.delivery: Over his shoulder, already going.

words.text: I'll get the deputy!
Somebody get the law... I'll go!
Where's the deputy? I'll find him.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He reaches the doctor: the man was shot and is breathing
lines.delivery: Blown from the run; the place first, then that he's alive.

words.text: Doc! Man shot, out front of {where}. He's breathing.
Doc, come quick! Man shot by {where}. He's breathing.
Doc! There's a man shot at {where}. He's breathing yet.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He reaches the doctor: the man is down, not shot (a fall, a blast), breathing
lines.delivery: As above.

words.text: Doc! Man down, out front of {where}. He's breathing.
Doc, come quick! A man's hurt by {where}. He's breathing.
Doc! A man's took bad at {where}. He's breathing yet.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He reaches the doctor: the man was shot and isn't breathing
lines.delivery: He knows the run was for nothing and comes anyway.

words.text: Doc! There's a man dead by {where}. Shot.
Doc, a man's been killed, out by {where}.
Doc, you'd best come anyhow. Man shot dead at {where}.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He reaches the doctor: the man isn't breathing, not shot
lines.delivery: As above.

words.text: Doc! There's a man dead by {where}.
Doc, there's a man lying dead at {where}. I don't know what done it.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He reaches Harlan (day 2 on): a man shot
lines.delivery: Says 'Deputy' like a man still getting used to it.

words.text: Deputy! Down at {where}, quick! A man's shot.
Deputy! You'd best come. There's trouble at {where}.
Deputy! There's a man shot at {where}.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: He reaches Harlan: a man down, not shot
lines.delivery: As above.

words.text: Deputy! You'd best come. There's trouble at {where}.
Deputy! Down at {where}, quick! A man's down.

scenes.title: The news, as a man has it
scenes.when: Any day, the hours and the morning after a shooting
scenes.reads: TownNews.line_of (src/people/town_news.gd) builds a man's line from his own version: one head line by what he holds (a killing, a shooting, a man down, shots), then at most one of 'who drew first' or 'how many shots', then who told him. The most specific id with words first (news.killing.you, then news.killing); a wording by his seed, so three men who counted three shots say it three ways. Slots: {who} who fired (by TownNews.name_of: Earl, Cody, Doc, 'the new man' or 'the deputy', else 'the storekeeper'), {whom} who was hit ('a man' if he doesn't know), {where}, {shots} ('three shots'), {teller}. A sentence that starts with a slot gets its capital.
scenes.setting: A calm townsman near Harlan says his own news once, before his ordinary line; two townsmen telling each other say the same lines to each other. A version is only what that man sensed: a slot he didn't fill isn't spoken.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: Harlan killed a man; said to Harlan's face
lines.delivery: Not an accusation. He's telling the man what the town has, to see what the man does with it.

words.text: You shot {whom} dead, by {where}.
You shot {whom}, out by {where}. He's dead, you know.
You shot {whom} dead at {where}. I was there.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: a killing, he has who did it
lines.delivery: Leans in. Pleased to be the one who has it.

words.text: {who} shot {whom} dead, out by {where}.
{who} killed {whom}. Shot him, at {where}.
{whom}'s dead. {who} shot him, by {where}.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: a killing, nobody seen firing
lines.delivery: He doesn't know, and minds not knowing.

words.text: Somebody's killed {whom}, by {where}.
{whom}'s been shot dead at {where}. Nobody's saying who.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: Harlan shot a man who lived; to his face
lines.delivery: As news.killing.you.

words.text: You shot {whom} by {where}.
You put a ball in {whom}, by {where}.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: a man shot, who did it
lines.delivery: As news.killing.

words.text: {who} shot {whom} by {where}.
{who} put a ball in {whom}, at {where}.
{whom} got shot by {where}. It was {who} done it.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: a man shot, nobody seen firing

words.text: {whom}'s been shot, by {where}.
Somebody shot {whom}, out by {where}.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: a man down, no shot he sensed

words.text: There's a man down by {where}.
A man went down by {where}. I never saw what took him.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: shots, nobody seen hit
lines.delivery: He only heard it. He keeps looking the way it came from.

words.text: Shooting, down by {where}. {shots}.
There was shooting by {where}. {shots}.
Somebody was shooting, out by {where}. {shots}, near as I could tell.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version told to Harlan's face: shots, nobody hit, and he saw it was Harlan (#1213)
lines.when: shots only; who Harlan; told to him

words.text: You let that iron off {at}. {shots}.
That was you, firing {at}. {shots}. I saw you.
You. Shooting {at}, like a damn fool. {shots}.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version: shots, nobody hit, and he saw who fired (#1213: witnesses said 'whoever it was')

words.text: {who} let off his iron {at}. {shots}.
It was {who}, shooting {at}. {shots}. I saw him.
{who} fired, {at}. {shots}, and nobody hurt, thank God.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: His version, told where it happened: shots, nobody seen hit, the shooter unseen (#1213: 'down by the saloon' from inside it)
lines.when: shots only; who empty; at the place

words.text: Shooting, right here. {shots}.
Somebody fired, right here. {shots}.
There was shooting right here. {shots}. Never saw who.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Tail: the man hit drew first, and he saw it
lines.delivery: He'll say it to anyone. He'd say it to a judge.

words.text: {whom} drew first. I saw it.
{whom} drew first. I'll swear to that.
It was {whom} drew first. I seen him.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Tail: the man hit drew first, by what he heard

words.text: {whom} drew first, I heard.
{whom} drew first, the way I heard it.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Tail: the man hit drew first, by what he was told

words.text: {whom} drew first, is what I'm told.
They say {whom} drew first.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Tail: more than one shot, and he heard them
lines.delivery: The number is his: he counted.

words.text: {shots}, I counted.
{shots}. I counted them.
I made it {shots}.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Tail: more than one shot, by what he was told

words.text: {shots}, they say.
{shots}, I'm told.
They say {shots}.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.delivery: Last, a little offhand.

words.text: {teller} told me.
I had it from {teller}.
That's what {teller} says, anyhow.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Opening a telling to another townsman (mostly walla under it)
lines.delivery: One clear opener; the rest is murmur.

words.text: You heard what happened?
You hear? Last night.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Asked (a look held at him), his version's slots empty

words.text: I only heard it. I never saw a thing.
Don't ask me. I was indoors with the shutters to.

scenes.title: The morning after, about Harlan
scenes.when: The day after Harlan shot a man in town
scenes.reads: Step 9 (regard and the barks) picks these by StoryState news.harlan, set overnight by TownNews: stopped_a_killer (the man he shot fired first, or had shot someone), shot_a_man, split (near even). Said as Harlan passes, or to him; only by a man whose own version has Harlan in it.
scenes.setting: Main Street, the morning after. No line names him.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.delivery: A touch of the hat; he isn't used to praising anybody.

words.text: Heard he pulled on you first. Nobody's grieving him.
Morning. That was a bad one you put down.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.delivery: Half to him, half to the woman beside her.

words.text: He'd shot one already, they say. Before you stopped him.

lines.speaker: barkeep
lines.delivery: Sets a glass down, and keeps his hand on the bottle.

words.text: This one's mine to stand.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Harlan passes; his view shot_a_man (not to his face)
lines.delivery: Said once Harlan is past, loud enough.

words.text: That's him. Shot a man in the street.
Shot him before he'd cleared leather, I heard.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.delivery: To a boy at the window, not to Harlan.

words.text: Come away from there. Come inside.

lines.speaker: storekeeper
lines.delivery: Doesn't look up from the ledger.

words.text: I'll have the money first, if it's the same to you.
Depends who you ask. Some say the other fellow pulled first.
I heard it both ways. I don't know as I believe either.

lines.speaker: loudmouth
lines.trigger: Harlan passes; split; the loudmouth on the walk
lines.delivery: To the whole walk.

words.text: I was told the fellow drew. Then I was told he never. Ask the deputy, he was stood right there, and I'd ask him myself only I'm busy.

scenes.title: The uneasy day
scenes.when: The day after a killing or a shooting the town holds (the calendar's `uneasy`)
scenes.reads: Step 9: barks by the day kind `uneasy` (valley_folk.json's kinds; StoryState news.yesterday = killing / shooting). Not after a story act's killing (No Law's morning is its own script).
scenes.setting: The storekeeper keeps in, the loudmouth's out on the walk telling it, the street's thinner.

lines.speaker: storekeeper
lines.delivery: Turning the sign, the bar in his other hand.

words.text: I'm barring the door tonight. You'd do the same.
Shutting early. It's nothing against you.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Wearing a pistol, at a lean spot
lines.delivery: Keeps touching it.

words.text: Never had cause to wear one in town before.
The wife made me put it on.

lines.speaker: loudmouth
lines.trigger: On the walk, anyone within 4 m

words.text: Somebody ought to do something about it, and I said so, I said it to the storekeeper this morning.
I'd have stopped it, if I'd been there. I was at my supper.
You stay in the yard today, you hear me?
Nobody's out. Even the dogs are under the porch.

scenes.title: The undertaker comes for a man
scenes.when: Any day, a man dead in town (ValleyFolk takes him to the undertaker's)
scenes.reads: When the undertaker's walk to a body is built (today the dead go once unseen, step 7's open), these are his: {whom} from his own version. No Law's Earl has his own lines (no_law.json morning.undertaker).
scenes.setting: The undertaker is exact; to him a dead man is a box, a name for the book and somebody to send the bill to.

lines.speaker: undertaker
lines.delivery: Already measuring him with his eye.

words.text: Stand away, please. Somebody take his feet.
I'll have him now. Mind his head on the step.

lines.speaker: undertaker
lines.trigger: At the body; his version has whom
lines.delivery: Writing it down.

words.text: {whom}. Shot. I'll want his other name for the book, if anybody has it.

lines.speaker: undertaker
lines.trigger: At the body; nobody knows him
lines.delivery: Looks round the ring of faces; nobody.

words.text: Anybody know him? No. Then he goes in the book as a stranger, and the county pays.

lines.speaker: undertaker
lines.trigger: At the body; Harlan near and the undertaker's version has Harlan firing
lines.delivery: Not unkind. He only wants it right for the book.

words.text: Yours, Deputy? I'll put it down that way.

scenes.title: An ordinary day
scenes.reads: Step 9 (the barks): by regard (warm, wary, cold, afraid), the hour and the spot.
scenes.setting: The street, the store, the livery.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.delivery: A nod with it.

words.text: Morning.
Morning, Deputy.
Hot enough to curl a board.
Wind's gone round. It'll blow dust all afternoon.

lines.speaker: storekeeper
lines.delivery: Not looking up from his ledger.

words.text: Directly. I'm in the middle of something.
Be with you directly.

lines.changed: 2026-11-23 (#1184: 'There's others before you' was said with nobody else there)

lines.speaker: storekeeper
lines.delivery: Through the glass.

words.text: We're shut.

lines.speaker: storekeeper
lines.trigger: You knock at the store's door in its hours
lines.delivery: Opening the door, wiping his hands.

words.text: Door sticks. Come on in.
We're open. What'll it be?

lines.speaker: loudmouth
lines.trigger: Carrying a sack, anyone within 4 m

words.text: Mind your feet. This ain't feathers.

scenes.title: Trouble in the street
scenes.when: Any day, shots or a fight
scenes.reads: Step 9, by Reaction's stages (CivilianBrain). The runner's own lines are scene `runner`.

words.text: That was a shot.
Up the street. Was that up the street?
Get in. Get in and shut it.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: At the ring round a man down, his version has no whom
lines.delivery: Up on his toes.

words.text: Who is it? Can you see who it is?

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: At the ring, his version has whom
lines.delivery: The name is the slot.

words.text: It's {whom}.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Sees a man down, somebody else is running

words.text: Somebody fetch Doc!

lines.speaker: barkeep
lines.trigger: A gun drawn in his room
lines.delivery: Both hands flat on the bar.

words.text: Put that up or get out.
Deputy... you've no call to point that here.

lines.speaker: loudmouth
lines.trigger: The ring round a fist fight

words.text: Let 'em have it out!
That'll do. That'll do, I said.
Is it done?
Is he gone?

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Coming out after (stage 4), having seen who fired (#1213: 'Is he gone?' with the shooter 6 m off)

words.text: Damn fool, firing off like that.
Somebody take that iron off him.
Is he done, you reckon?

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Coming out after (stage 4), the man who fired right there and in his sight (#1213)

words.text: You done? Lord.
Put that thing away, mister. Please.
What'd you go and do that for?

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.delivery: Holding a cup she isn't drinking.

words.text: Look at my hands. Look at them.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.trigger: At the ring, a child with her

words.text: Come away. That's nothing to look at.

scenes.title: The sheriff dying, the badge
scenes.when: Day 1 evening to the funeral; the badge from day 2
scenes.reads: Step 9. No Law's own town lines (no_law.json `town`, `morning`) come first where both fit.

words.text: He's poorly. Doc's not left him.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.delivery: Hat in his hand.

words.text: He's gone. This morning.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.delivery: To Harlan, quickly, then away.

words.text: You gave him a night with his wife.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: The mourning day, as Harlan passes
lines.delivery: Not to his face.

words.text: Some rode right by him, I hear.
Deputy, is it. Well.
I'm glad somebody's wearing it.
A nester wearing the sheriff's badge. A nester! I'll drink to that, I will.

lines.speaker: barkeep
lines.trigger: The badge, Cody not yet taken
lines.delivery: Wiping the same glass.

words.text: He'll walk back in here, you know. Bold as brass.

scenes.title: After No Justice
scenes.reads: Step 9, by StoryState nojustice.ending, nojustice.jail, nojustice.bodies; kett.loose by C8 a (PROPOSED on #830). Nobody in town says the prisoner's name (K3).
scenes.setting: Pick 2 (Sean, #851, A): after the prisoner is turned loose the town splits: some stand by Harlan, others say he should have finished it. Pick 3 (Sean, #851): the town only knows what it can find; found or not, it assumes Joe did it.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Arrest, the prisoner in the cell

words.text: You brought him in alive. I'd not have troubled.

lines.speaker: townswoman
lines.delivery: Peering at the jail's window.

words.text: Is that him? He don't look like much, behind a door.
He eats what the house eats. He'll not thank me.
And when his friends come for him?

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: The prisoner turned loose (pick 2 A: for Harlan)

words.text: You brought him in. What the Army done after ain't on you.

lines.speaker: loudmouth
lines.trigger: The prisoner turned loose (pick 2 A: against)

words.text: Should've left him up there with the others.
They let him go? After all that?
That's him. Walking about like he owns the street.
Five. And one of them won't bear looking at.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Revenge, the bodies found; his liking of Harlan high

words.text: Whoever did it saved the county the cost of a trial.
Cut like that. Lord.
You were up there, Deputy. Who took his hair?

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Revenge, the bodies not found (pick 3: the town assumes)

words.text: That Ute that rode out with the deputy. Anybody seen him since?

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: The prisoner killed in the fight

words.text: Went up there with one man and came back. I'll say that for him.

lines.speaker: undertaker
lines.trigger: Harlan shot him; the undertaker has seen the body
lines.delivery: Evidence spoken by the one man who'd see it (DESIGN §10).

words.text: Powder on his shirt front. He was shot close, Deputy.

scenes.title: The saloon at night
scenes.when: Any night, 19:00 to 02:00, in the room
scenes.reads: Step 10 (SaloonRoom, src/people/saloon_room.gd): the room's director gives a bit to a man who's there and he says its line (`on` room.toast, room.hail, room.leave, room.answer, room.glass), by the barks' rules (once a day a person, not a line another said within the minute). Laughs, coughs and talk have no words.
scenes.setting: The brief's §6: every distinct sound in the room comes from a person, and he does it. A toast: he lifts his glass and the bar lifts theirs. A hail: a man at the bar to one coming in. Night 1 (No Law) the room is a little bold; the night the sheriff dies it is louder than ever (Sean's pick 4 C, #851).

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: A man at the bar, to a named man coming in (Earl)
lines.delivery: Across the room, glad of him.

words.text: Hey, {whom}!
{whom}! Get in here.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: A man at the bar, to anyone else coming in
lines.delivery: Loud, friendly.

words.text: Hey, you old thief!
Look what the wind blew in.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Harlan comes in, the town warm to him, the badge on
lines.delivery: One word and a lifted hand. The brief's third night: the town's answer in one doorway.

words.text: Deputy.
Evening, Deputy.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: Harlan comes in, the town warm to him, no badge yet

words.text: Evening.
Come in out of the dark, mister.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: A man at the bar lifts his glass; the bar lifts theirs
lines.delivery: Short. Said to the glass as much as the room.

words.text: Here's how.
Here's luck.
To the last one. And the next.

lines.speaker: loudmouth
lines.trigger: The loudmouth's toast, night 1 (No Law, before the murder)
lines.when: the sheriff shot and lying at Doc's, nobody killed yet
lines.delivery: No Law's town.bold (no_law.json), said here as his toast: the same words, kept in step with that line.

words.text: Ain't no sheriff tonight, boys!
Who's going to fine me? Doc?

lines.speaker: loudmouth
lines.trigger: The loudmouth's toast, the night the sheriff dies
lines.delivery: Too loud. Half the bar drinks to it, half looks at its boots.

words.text: To the sheriff. He ain't here to mind the noise.
Sheriff's dead, boys. Who's going to tell us it's late?

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.trigger: A man going home: drains it, hat on
lines.delivery: Over his shoulder.

words.text: Night, all.
That's me. Night.

lines.speaker: townsman
lines.delivery: Not looking up.

words.text: Night.
Mind the step.

lines.speaker: barkeep
lines.trigger: He sets a glass down before Harlan unasked
lines.when: his own regard warm, Harlan at the bar, once a night
lines.delivery: Aggrieved even when he's being kind: he's counted what it costs him.

words.text: On the house. Just the one, mind.
That one's mine. The next is yours.

scenes.title: An ordinary day in the street
scenes.reads: TownBarks `pass` (#1184): each man's own lines by his job (his pools), the hour and his spot, any regard but the cold and the afraid for the friendly ones; the gate's second round had one to four lines in ten minutes.

words.text: Coffee's in. Flour's late. Same as every week.
Freight wagon's due Thursday, if the road holds.
Dust comes back faster than I can sweep it.
Mind the step. I've just wet it.
These crates don't get any lighter.
Nails, lamp oil, and a sack of something nobody ordered.
Slow today. Folks are keeping their money in their boots.
If you're buying, I'm selling. If you're looking, look quick.
Near closing. Whatever you want, want it now.
Shutting up shop directly.
Grey mare threw a shoe again. Smith'll love that.
Morning. Hay's gone up a nickel.
Horses have more sense than half this town.
That bay's been kicking the boards all day. Don't stand behind him.
Feed and a stall, two bits a night. Less if you muck it yourself.
Wind's got the horses jumpy.
Stand off the anvil. I don't want to burn you.
Iron's the only thing in this town that does what it's told.
Fire's lit before the rooster. Every day.
Morning. Bring me anything bent and I'll make it straight.
Livery owes me for four shoes. Don't tell him I said.
Hands like these, and they want me to write my name neat.
Keep your feet dry and your powder drier.
Nobody's sick today. I don't trust it.
Morning. If you're bleeding, come by. If you're not, good.
Morning. Sleep, if you can get it. Best medicine I've got.

words.text: Forgive me. I measure folk by eye. Habit.
Quiet week. Good news for everybody but me.
Don't suppose there's any work in this town.
I've seen worse towns. Not many.
Just holding up the wall. It'd fall without me.
Sun's warm. Wall's warm. I'm not moving.
Boots off my rug. I mean it.
Rooms are fifty cents. Clean sheets are extra, and worth it.
I've two rooms empty, if you know anybody respectable.
Supper's at six. Late is cold.
Too early for the piano. Too late for church.
You're not buying, you're just looking. I know the type.
It's quiet till sundown. Then it's not.
Buy a girl a sarsaparilla? No? Suit yourself.
Bar's open. Whiskey's two bits, and it isn't worth it.
Glasses don't clean themselves. More's the pity.
This town's dead as a doornail till payday.
I could lift that wagon. Bet me a dollar.
Hot as the hinges out here. Somebody stand me a beer.
Noon, and not a drop taken. A man could die.
Best seat in town. Free, too.
Sit down, sit down. The bench don't bite.
Dry as a bone. We could use a rain.
Looks like weather out west.
Morning.
Mm. Morning.

lines.speaker: townsman

words.text: Dinner bell's gone. Too hot to eat.
Sun's straight up. Not a lick of shade.
Half the town's at its dinner. The other half wants to be.

words.text: Long afternoon.
Same as yesterday. Hotter.
Evening.
Getting on for supper.
Sit if you like. Bench don't belong to me.
I'm resting my feet. They've earned it.
Can't stop. I'm behind already.
Busy. Talk later.
Waiting on the mail. It's always late.
Just seeing who's about.
Morning. Mind the mud by the trough.
Morning. You're up early.
Don't block the walk, please.

Evening to you.

scenes.title: Neighbours
scenes.when: Any day, two men within a few metres of each other
scenes.reads: ValleyFolk._chat_step (#1184): two calm day men by each other, you within earshot: one says a `chat` line, the other answers with a `chat.reply` a beat on.
scenes.setting: Walks, benches, the livery, the bar.

words.text: Flour's up again. Robbery, plain and simple.
You seen the price of coffee? I'll drink water.
Rain by Sunday. You mark me.
Creek's lower than I've ever seen it.
Railroad man was in again, asking after land.
They say the line's coming through north of the creek.
Baron's men moved a herd past the creek last night.
Saw dust on the east road. Cattle, a lot of 'em.
My wife says I talk too much. I told her she don't listen.
Wife's sister's coming. For a month.
Lost four dollars to Earl last night. Four!
That drifter plays cards like he's got nowhere to be.
They say the mine's hiring again.
Miner come in with a poke of dust yesterday. Spent it all by dark.
Stage brought no mail again. Three weeks.
Letter come for the widow Pratt. Nobody wants to take it up.
Preacher's coming through next month, if he don't get lost again.
Church roof wants fixing before the snow.
Your account's at nine dollars. I'm only saying.
Got a bolt of blue calico in. Pretty, if you like blue.
Bring it round after dinner and I'll true it up.
That wheel's got a cracked felloe. It'll go on you.
Feed bill's due. I'm not a charity.
Your horse ate more'n you did this week.
I'll tell you what this town needs. A second saloon.
I arm-wrestled a mule skinner in Abilene. Beat him twice.
The Pratt girl's walking out with the bank clerk.
I'd not let a daughter of mine near that saloon.
Hens have stopped laying. It's the heat.
Did you hear the dog howling half the night?

words.text: Beer's warm. Ice wagon never came.
Swept this floor twice today and it's still dirty.

That so.

Ha! That'll be the day.

True enough.
